mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger occurs, or the effect reverses in a high-inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when unemployment is simultaneously falling rapidly.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% month-over-month, sustained for two months, indicates supply-side stress that raises input costs and reduces earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m change < -1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect is absent during periods of falling commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, compressing real yields and eroding corporate profit margins, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such co-triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when GDP growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A strong, sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above trend by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > trend +10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous fall in both UNRATE and PAYEMS below their 12-month averages signals a broad-based labor market deterioration, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both below 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such co-triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio above its 5-year median for six consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary savings and lower marginal propensity to consume, which depresses near-term demand and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio above 5-year median for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rapid credit expansion.
